newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end flat in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end flat in quiet trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed almost unchanged on Monday in quiet trading, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.01 pct to 101.57
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct to 101.0.
Volume was low at 122 million shekels.
"The market is very quiet and most issues closed almost unchanged. Yields fell sharply before the end of the year and bonds are less interesting now," said a trader at Bank Leumi.

"Yields on CPI-linked bonds continue to decline but at a very slow pace. Yields fell to 4.4-4.44 percent and I believe that they will not decline much further," said Irit Ben-Zur-Gil at Sahar Securities.
Traders said that unlinked bonds closed almost unchanged.
"Yields on unlinked bonds fell sharply and these bonds are not attractive for institutional investors anymore," Ben-Zur-Gil added.

"Israeli banks reduced the interest on short-term deposits and private investors are moving to Makams. The rise of the makam pushed yields lower to 13.84 percent which is not attractive for investors who predict a 1997 inflation of more than nine percent," Ben-Zur-Gil said.
Traders noted that dollar-linked bonds rose sharply following the rise of the U.S. currency to a new multi-year high in world markets.
In the local foreign currency market the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2870 shekels against 3.2700 shekels on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
